output.summary: The run is VALID but the window verdict is NO_VERDICT. The business policy FAILs: overall error_rate_ratio is 2312/37841 (~6.1%) against a 1% (0.01) threshold, with all 2,312 errors found in the "checkout" transaction (2,312 of 6,515 samples) and logged as frontend.request_error by the frontend service between epoch 1790632254832 and 1790632369669. The resource aspect is NO_VERDICT: paymentservice cpu, memory, and cpu-throttle-ratio series are missing 4 of 23 cells (RESOURCE_GAPS / MISSING_SAMPLES), the cpu-throttle-ratio policy check is NO_VERDICT due to MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS, and the wrapper analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE (RESOURCE_GAPS, MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS, SOURCE_ACQUISITION_PARTIAL). A resource threshold finding shows paymentservice cpu-throttle-ratio exceeding 0.2 in cells 1790632350000-1790632380000 (observed max 0.56895862409), but completeness gaps and unverified clock alignment (clock_alignment = not_verified_by_core) prevent any causal or temporal claim. Advice is limited to hypotheses to test, not proven causes, and does not change the recorded NO_VERDICT.

hypotheses.observation: The overall summary reports 2,312 errors out of 39,099 samples, and the checkout transaction summary reports the same 2,312 errors out of 6,515 samples, while the other transactions (add product to cart, cart, home, product, reset cart) each report 0 errors. The OpenSearch errors result groups all 2,312 errors as frontend.request_error from service frontend, with first error at 1790632254832 and last error at 1790632369669.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The business FAIL is driven entirely by checkout requests failing at the frontend as 'request error'; this could reflect a backend dependency invoked only by checkout, but no evidence identifies which call or component failed.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Take a sample of the failed checkout documents from the error result and follow them into frontend logs/traces to identify the failing downstream call during the error window; confirm each error corresponds to the checkout sampler before attributing root cause.

hypotheses.recommended_check: Obtain a complete paymentservice cpu-throttle-ratio series without missing cells, verify clock alignment first, then overlay the series against the checkout error timeline (1790632245000-1790632380000) to test overlap before concluding any relationship.

caveats: The recorded verdict is NO_VERDICT and this advice does not change it; business FAIL and resource NO_VERDICT are separate statuses and NO_POLICY/missing data are not passes.
Analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE with reasons RESOURCE_GAPS, MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS, and SOURCE_ACQUISITION_PARTIAL, so conclusions about paymentservice are provisional.
The policy-check denominator (37,841) differs from the overall metric summary sample count (39,099); these are distinct measurement scopes and should not be treated as identical.
Paymentservice cpu, cpu-throttle-ratio, and memory are missing 4 of 23 cells; missing samples and gaps do not prove the absence of contention or throttling outside the observed cells.
Latency percentiles (e.g., overall p99 179 ms, checkout p99 100 ms, max ~1006 ms) are not joined to error samples, so no latency-to-error relationship can be asserted.
The throttle-ratio finding and the error timeline come from sources whose clock alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no lead/lag or temporal causal claim is supported.
Error log samples contain only the message 'request error' with no further detail; the root cause of the 2,312 checkout failures is not identified by the evidence.
All hypotheses above are explanations to test, not proven causes; the evidence only supports comparisons of counts, ratios, thresholds, and coverage, not causal attribution.
